questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The academic level at the University of Copenhagen is already quite high, so I didn't decide to go to abroad for those reasons. Instead I hoped that having completed an exchange semester in another country, would provide me with a more international profil.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was amazing!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It's quite hard to find everything and there is a lot of information. Especially at Sorbonne where it's mostly in French.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We received an introduction on the first day in one of the halls. Other than that, we continuously received some information online.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It was difficult to receive information and Sorbonne is a difficult place. Luckily one is away with other Danes, so you pretty quickly figure it all out by relying on each other.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very easy. I applied only to one place, the Danish house in the Cité and I got in.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You risk getting a bit isolated from the rest of Paris. You can end up living in a bobble.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I lived in the Danish House in the Cité Universitaire. It was simply amazing. Great accommodation, nice room, fantastic kitchen, great people. Highly recommend it. Its awesome.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It's weird at Sorbonne, basically you write to a Professor like "Hey can I join your class" and then usually say yes. Then you send the teachers response to the administration etc etc.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Just did above.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Other Danes! Other than that, you figure it out, you can contact the administration and they sort of explain it

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It took a little while, but I ended up in all the classes I wanted to.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Pray to the French Gods and be calm, know it eventually all works out.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was a lot of good academic courses.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level at the University of Copenhagen imo was generally higher. Sorbonne's history and English department is more like how you imagine universities were in the 19th century. Some professors like to be the only one to talk, and others want a lot of discussions. Some of these discussions are more interesting than others. We had one professor, very disorganized, who asked questions like "What is democracy?" When questions are this open, the class discussion becomes unproductive.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Answered that above.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Brexit 
Relation International 
Satire de Byron et Swift
New Perspectives in American Religion

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Brexit was amazing. Madame Charlotte, Professor of British Civilisation is a fantastic teacher.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Paris is expensive. Make sure you apply for funding.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food! Food was expensive, Especially if you wanted to (you want to) eat out once in a while.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: You have to sign up FAST!!! Otherwise all the slots are filled up at the university and then there is no getting in. They are tough !

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Football, chess, all kinds of sports, board game nights etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Take a language course through Sorobnne.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: It's Paris, a million things to do. Jazz clubs, running in the local parks, see a movie, go to the fantastic bookstores in the 5th arrondissement.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy because I lived in the Cite Universitiare with other international young students

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Speak with them from the beginning, do not care about it being awkward. Ask them questions, and just keep going. Rather be that annoying Erasmus person who talks too much but gain 3 friends, than be silent and gain none.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I had been to France a few times before so I didn't really notice that many differences. But Paris is a big city, way bigger than Copenhagen. So be prepared for living in a big city.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their love of books. In Denmark books are expensive and always new. Hard to find old ones. In Paris it's everywhere especially archive books. The Food is great. And the University offers more of a personal connection to students (at least in the English department) You can talk more with Professors and develop more than in Copenhagen.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Never speak English with people in Paris when you are out. If they speak English with you, just tell them you don't speak English. They won't believe you, but they will at least keep speaking French so you can practise. 
2. Sign up for social clubs and activities at Sorbonne right away. Spots get taken up fast.
3. Decide if you want to live in Cite Universitaire or not. There are positives and negatives to both. Cité gives you instant friends and parties. But you are not truly immersed in Parisian culture. The opposite is true for living outside Cite-.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Speaking French with friends. Presenting in French. Meeting new people who are all incredibly talented. it's crazy in the city. people are either Phd students, singers, or able to speak a million languages. You will feel stupid compared to them, but that's great too.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Adjusting to life in Paris, its a huge city after all

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
